kind: project development diagnostics, not a replication

foregroundPreference.scope: named foreground region on named background

controls: fixed copy, geometry, area, adjacency and viewing size
rationale hidden until visual ratings fixed

cases.question: Does coherence change without losing brief fit?
cases.hypothesis: A more related supporting family may help a disconnected treatment; no forced winner.

cases.question: Does the composition improve without destroying its mood?
cases.hypothesis: A value adjustment may solve dullness without adding hue; verify delivered luminance and functional contrast.

cases.change: background hue, in separate low/high lightness-difference blocks
cases.hold: named foreground color, area, composition and chroma where in gamut
cases.question: Do focal liking and whole-pair liking diverge, and does the pattern depend on lightness?
cases.hypothesis: Contrasting backgrounds are candidates, not presumed improvements; report gamut or luminance confounds.

cases.question: Does the same color set work differently in different roles?
cases.hypothesis: Role assignment may matter; do not count swapped displays as equivalent.

analysis: Keep every target separate; report per-brief paired differences, ties, disagreement and uncertainty. No combined beauty score. Model-critic feedback is not human validation. Confirm ground/foreground labels before interpreting results.
gates: independent reviewer actually sees live rendered pixels
required functional contrast and non-color cues cannot be waived
blocked visual access means not run
no preference ledger entry without actual user evidence
limits: No candidates or participants yet; no effect demonstrated.
These cases are visible development tasks, not held out.
Munsell/BCP findings are not numeric OKLCH prediction coefficients.
A simple pair diagnostic cannot certify a multi-color narrative composition.
